title: Kafka Producers and Consumers
summary: Publish and consume digest events with agreed serialization and explicit acknowledgment boundaries.

sources.title: Engineering Digest: What is Kafka ? How to use Confluent Kafka in Spring Boot Application ?

richText: Separate event creation from processing
Kafka stores records in topics. A producer writes records. A consumer reads records and performs work.
A topic is divided into partitions. Records have offsets that identify their position within a partition. Kafka ordering applies within a partition.
A consumer group shares partitions among its consumers. Another group can read the same topic independently for a different purpose.
Use Kafka when work can happen later, multiple services need the event, or a backlog must survive a temporarily unavailable consumer.
A weekly digest producer can queue summaries while an email consumer sends them. Broker acknowledgment confirms the configured publish acknowledgment, not email delivery.
The examples use Spring Boot 3, Spring Kafka 3+, and Java 17. Add spring-kafka and let Boot manage compatible library versions.
Match producer and consumer formats
A serializer converts a Java value to bytes. A deserializer converts received bytes back into a value. Both sides must agree on the format.
This example uses text JSON and StringSerializer/StringDeserializer. Define an event ID and a versioned JSON contract before adding more event fields.

For a local broker, bootstrap servers can be localhost:9092. For Confluent Cloud, use its provided bootstrap address, SASL_SSL authentication, and generated client settings. Keep credentials in environment configuration.

spring.kafka.bootstrap-servers=${KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS}
spring.kafka.producer.key-serializer=org.apache.kafka.common.serialization.StringSerializer
spring.kafka.producer.value-serializer=org.apache.kafka.common.serialization.StringSerializer
spring.kafka.consumer.key-deserializer=org.apache.kafka.common.serialization.StringDeserializer
spring.kafka.consumer.value-deserializer=org.apache.kafka.common.serialization.StringDeserializer
spring.kafka.consumer.enable-auto-commit=false
spring.kafka.consumer.auto-offset-reset=earliest
Wait for the publish result
The key user-42 normally keeps that user’s records in the same partition while the partitioning configuration stays unchanged.
send returns a CompletableFuture in Spring Kafka 3+. A return from send alone does not prove the broker acknowledged the record.

The example blocks up to five seconds. Its containing method must handle InterruptedException, ExecutionException, and TimeoutException. Alternatively, attach a completion callback and persist the outcome.
Read the event in a listener
Add the listener to a Spring bean. Here digestProcessor parses the JSON, checks its contract, and submits the digest email. Keep that application logic in a service.
A successful listener return permits offset progress under the container acknowledgment policy. Let processing errors reach the container so retry and recovery can run.
earliest applies when the group has no valid committed offset. It does not replay all records on every restart.
A crash after submitting email but before offset commit can cause redelivery. Track event IDs and understand the mail provider’s duplicate handling.
